title: Left derived functor on the derived category computed by a resolving class
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K(\mathcal A)$ its homotopy category of cochain complexes and $Q:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $F:K(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D'$ be an exact functor of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Suppose $\mathcal P$ is a class of complexes such that (1) for every complex $X$ there is a quasi-isomorphism $X'\to X$ with $X'\in\mathcal P$, and (2) for every quasi-isomorphism $s:X\to X'$ with $X,X'\in\mathcal P$ the morphism $F(s)$ is an isomorphism. Then $F$ has an everywhere defined left derived functor $LF:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D'$ with a natural transformation $\varepsilon:LF\circ Q\to F$, universal among pairs $(G,\ G\circ Q\to F)$ (a right Kan extension of $F$ along $Q$); $LF$ is an exact functor of triangulated categories; and for every $X\in\mathcal P$ the component $\varepsilon_X:LF(QX)\to F(X)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XN (derived-lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part, in Situation Tag 05S8 with D = K(A) and S the quasi-isomorphisms; exactness from Proposition Tag 05SE (derived-proposition-derived-functor), the statement for LF; the universal property is equation (derived-equation-everywhere) and Definition Tag 05S9

proof.text: For each complex $X$, consider the category of quasi-isomorphisms into $X$. By (1), the full subcategory of arrows $X'\to X$ with $X'\in\mathcal P$ is cofinal; by (2), $F$ is constant up to canonical isomorphism on this subcategory. Hence the pro-object used in the resolving-class criterion (Tag 05S9) is essentially constant with value $F(X')$ (and for $X\in\mathcal P$ the identity resolution may be used). Thus a pointwise left derived functor exists at every $X$, and every $X\in\mathcal P$ computes it.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06XN proof, dual resolving-class argument

proof.text: By the Stacks-to-Kan bridge, the essentially constant pro-object in Definition 05S9 obtained in Step 1 is exactly a pointwise right Kan extension at $QX$, with the same value and comparison map.

source.place: Definition Tag 05S9 and Lemma Tag 05SA, pointwise reformulation in Situation Tag 05S8

proof.text: Apply the pointwise-to-global derived-functor construction: the pointwise existence from Step 2 and the localization $Q$ give a left derived functor $LF:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal D'$ with a natural transformation $LF\circ Q\to F$ exhibiting the right Kan extension and universal property.

The quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ satisfy the saturated multiplicative-system and triangulation-compatibility hypotheses of Situation 05S8. Together with the bridge, the pointwise Kan-extension functor just constructed is the Stacks left derived functor defined everywhere, so Proposition Tag 05SE (LF part), as stated in the exactness node, makes $LF$ exact. For $X\in\mathcal P$, the component of the canonical transformation is an isomorphism by the identity resolution in Step 1 and the comparison clause of the bridge; therefore $LF(QX)\cong F(X)$.
